name: CompCert verified compiler
artifact: The verified compilation pipeline from typed CompCert C abstract syntax to target Asm for AArch64, ARM, PowerPC, RISC-V, and x86.
spec: For every source program S and generated program C, if compilation succeeds, every observable behavior of C is allowed by (or improves on an allowed behavior of) S. The whole-compiler result composes semantic-preservation proofs for the verified passes over their formal small-step semantics.
theorem: transf_c_program_correct; separate-compilation linking results in Compiler.v
assumptions: Correctness is relative to the formal source/target semantics. Coq's kernel, extraction/runtime, assembler, linker, and execution hardware remain trusted at their respective boundaries.
excludes: Preprocessing, parsing, type checking/elaboration before the source AST, assembling and linking are not covered by the central end-to-end theorem.

name: CertiKOS mC2 kernel/hypervisor
artifact: A multicore concurrent kernel/hypervisor assembled from certified abstraction layers and compiled with CompCert.
spec: Each implementation layer contextually refines its abstract machine: every observable behavior of the concrete concurrent layer is permitted by the abstract layer. Layer composition connects x86/Clight implementation modules to the top-level concurrent kernel interface, yielding functional-correctness and isolation consequences stated by the model.
theorem: Certified contextual-refinement chain between concurrent abstraction layers
assumptions: Relies on the modeled x86 machine, hardware/environment assumptions, the Coq kernel, and trusted boot/device portions outside the certified layers.
excludes: Not a proof of commodity guest OS correctness or all device firmware/hardware behavior.

name: FSCQ file system
artifact: A Unix-like file system implementation written with extraction to executable code.
spec: Crash Hoare Logic triples relate normal execution to the abstract file-system state and every possible crash point to a crash condition. After any sequence of crashes and recoveries, recovery re-establishes the representation invariant and exposes a state allowed by the abstract specification, preventing loss beyond the operations permitted by that specification.
theorem: CHL operation and recovery theorems for FSCQ
assumptions: The disk model (including atomic-sector behavior), extracted-code/runtime path, and platform are trusted boundaries.
excludes: Does not prove physical media reliability, application-level durability absent required calls, or correctness outside the modeled API and crash model.

name: Fiat Cryptography arithmetic routines
artifact: Generated C code for prime-field arithmetic used by cryptographic implementations.
spec: Generated routines refine mathematical modular arithmetic: for inputs satisfying representation bounds, operations such as add, subtract, multiply, square, and inversion return an encoded value congruent to the corresponding operation in Z/pZ, with proved bounds needed by subsequent routines. Synthesis preserves these functional specifications through word-level transformations.
theorem: Per-curve/generated-pipeline correctness lemmas and bounds proofs
assumptions: Coq kernel and the compilation chain from generated C to machine code; constant-time claims require the documented syntactic/compilation discipline.
excludes: Field arithmetic correctness alone is not a proof of an entire cryptographic protocol, key management, entropy, or side-channel freedom of a deployed binary.

name: HACL*/EverCrypt Curve25519 Coq validation
artifact: Selected field-arithmetic implementations in the HACL*/EverCrypt ecosystem connected to Coq/Fiat-Crypto proofs.
spec: For supported generated field operations, the implementation result represents the corresponding operation modulo 2^255−19 and respects carry/limb bounds. The Coq contribution applies to the identified arithmetic components, while much of HACL* is verified in F* and therefore is outside this catalog's Lean/Coq claim.
theorem: Fiat-Crypto field-operation correctness instantiated for Curve25519
assumptions: The integration glue and downstream C toolchain are separate trusted links unless compiled through a verified path.
excludes: Not a claim that all HACL*/EverCrypt code is proved in Coq.

name: Verdi Raft
artifact: A Raft consensus implementation in the Verdi framework, extractable to executable OCaml.
spec: Under the framework's network/failure semantics, reachable states satisfy Raft safety invariants including state-machine safety: committed log entries at a given index agree, and applied outputs are consistent with the replicated state-machine log. Verified system transformers preserve specified trace properties while adding network mechanisms.
theorem: Raft linearizability/state-machine-safety invariant chain in VerdiRaft
assumptions: Safety is relative to the formal asynchronous network and crash/reboot models; extraction, runtime shims, OS, and network stack are trusted.
excludes: The main safety result is not an unconditional liveness theorem under arbitrary partitions.

name: Verdi LockServ
spec: For every reachable network state in the modeled semantics, no two distinct clients simultaneously own the lock (mutual exclusion). A liveness variant proves progress under its labeled-network fairness premises.
assumptions: Formal network semantics and stated fairness premises; extracted OCaml runtime and transport shim.
excludes: No timing, Byzantine-fault, or real transport-stack guarantee.

name: Verdi VarD primary-backup key-value store
artifact: VarD key-value server transformed with sequence numbering and asynchronous primary-backup replication.
spec: The transformed network's externally visible traces refine those of the ideal key-value service for the modeled failures; sequence numbering suppresses duplicate effects and the primary-backup transformer preserves the source system's trace property.
theorem: Correctness of SeqNum and PrimaryBackup verified system transformers, instantiated by VarD
assumptions: The Verdi network semantics and transformer premises; extracted runtime and shim.
excludes: Not Byzantine tolerant and not a performance or availability guarantee under indefinite failure.

name: VST verified C components
artifact: C functions verified in the Verified Software Toolchain against CompCert Clight semantics, including the SHA-256 implementation case study.
spec: A function body satisfies a separation-logic funspec: from its precondition over values, permissions, and memory resources, every defined execution meets the postcondition and preserves the framed resources. Soundness connects semax proofs to CompCert's operational semantics; CompCert transports behavior properties to assembly.
theorem: semax_body judgments and VST soundness; SHA256 functional-correctness theorem
assumptions: Correct formal specification, CompCert semantics/toolchain boundary, external-call models, and Coq kernel.
excludes: VST does not make arbitrary C programs verified; each implementation requires a completed proof against an adequate specification.

name: bedrock2 compiler and device software
artifact: A low-level imperative language, compiler to RISC-V, and verified routines/drivers used in embedded stacks.
spec: Compiled execution simulates the source operational semantics: subject to memory and external-call premises, successful source steps are matched by RISC-V machine execution with corresponding traces/results. Individual programs carry Hoare-style functional specifications over memory and I/O traces.
assumptions: RISC-V machine model, device/external-call specifications, assembler/linker/load path as documented, and Coq kernel.
excludes: A driver proof covers the modeled device contract, not undocumented physical-device behavior.

name: Kami hardware components
artifact: Parameterized hardware modules expressed in Kami and compiled toward RTL.
spec: A concrete module refines an abstract module when every observable labeled behavior of the implementation is matched by the specification under the defined simulation relation. Modular refinement rules compose proofs across module connections and rule scheduling.
theorem: trace/refinement theorems for Kami modules and compiler transformations
assumptions: Correctness is relative to Kami semantics and the documented extraction/RTL/toolchain boundary.
excludes: Does not by itself establish physical timing, power, fabrication, or analog properties.

name: Perennial/Goose storage components
artifact: Go programs translated by Goose, including crash-safe storage case studies; the historical system uses Coq/Iris and current primary development uses Lean/iris-lean.
spec: Concurrent separation-logic Hoare triples establish functional correctness and linearizability; crash weakest preconditions quantify over crashes at any step and require recovery to re-establish the durable invariant. Mailboat's stated contract ensures delivered messages remain durable after recovery and readers observe only complete messages.
theorem: Per-function wp theorems; crash-recovery and durable-invariant proofs
assumptions: Goose semantics/translation, modeled filesystem API and crash behavior, language/runtime/compiler boundary, and proof-assistant kernel.
excludes: Current Lean branch explicitly excludes crash/recovery reasoning; historical crash proofs are in Coq. Untranslated Go and the Go runtime are not automatically verified.

name: DaisyNFS
artifact: A concurrent crash-safe network file server written in Go/Goose.
spec: Operations are logically atomic with respect to an abstract file-system state; completed operations survive crashes according to the durable specification; recovery re-establishes the representation invariant; concurrent executions refine the abstract API under the modeled network and disk semantics.
theorem: Perennial linearizability and crash-safety theorems for DaisyNFS
assumptions: Goose/Go correspondence and compiler/runtime, filesystem/disk and network models, and Coq kernel.
excludes: No proof of real disks, NICs, Go runtime, or arbitrary unmodeled failures.

name: GoJournal
artifact: A concurrent write-ahead logging library implemented in Go/Goose.
spec: Committed transactions refine atomic updates to an abstract durable state; after a crash, recovery produces either the pre-transaction or committed state as allowed by the log protocol, while concurrent clients see behavior consistent with the library's logically atomic specification.
theorem: Perennial crash-safety and logically atomic specs for journal operations
assumptions: Modeled block/file API and crash semantics, Goose translation/runtime, and Coq kernel.
excludes: Does not cover physical failures beyond the storage model.

name: IronKV/Verdi key-value service
artifact: A key-value service expressed as Verdi handlers and transformed into a fault-tolerant network implementation.
spec: For the modeled input/output traces, the implementation refines the sequential key-value state machine: read responses agree with the latest permitted write and replication/sequence-number transformations preserve the application invariant.
theorem: VarD invariant plus transformer trace-correctness instantiations
assumptions: Verdi's fault/network models and trusted extracted runtime.
excludes: Not a statement about Byzantine clients, arbitrary storage corruption, or liveness during permanent partitions.

name: Lean 4 compiler bootstrap correctness components
artifact: Selected Lean compiler transformations and runtime/library algorithms carrying internal theorems.
spec: Individual verified transformations prove equivalence or refinement between their input and output representations under Lean-defined semantics; the Lean kernel checks these propositions. This entry deliberately does not assert that the complete native-code compiler or runtime is end-to-end verified.
theorem: Component-specific correctness theorems in the Lean 4 source tree
assumptions: Lean kernel implementation, axioms used by a theorem, code generator, C compiler and runtime where executable behavior is claimed.
excludes: Lean's implementation documentation does not support calling the entire Lean compiler/runtime formally verified.

name: Lean protocol support examples
artifact: Executable protocol models and proofs built with Galois's Lean protocol-support library.
spec: Protocol implementations are transition systems; invariant proofs show every reachable global network state satisfies the stated safety property, reduced through compositional lemmas to local component transitions.
assumptions: The selected network transition semantics and environment assumptions; extraction/runtime are outside model-level claims.
excludes: A verified protocol model is not automatically a proof of an unrelated production implementation.

name: LeanOS verified kernel models
artifact: Executable kernel-interface and device-policy reference models paired with a bootable experimental kernel.
spec: Named Lean theorems establish pre/postconditions, state invariants, finite policy confinement, and deterministic scenario properties of the reference models. The project explicitly labels the C executor connection as tested rather than a proved full refinement.
theorem: Repository claim-index theorems, checked with no admitted placeholders in the indexed modules
assumptions: Lean code generation, generated C, C compiler, handwritten C/assembly, linker, firmware/emulator/hardware, and model-to-executor correspondence remain in the TCB or test boundary.
excludes: The maintainers explicitly state that this is not yet a verified operating system and does not prove the resulting machine code or general concurrency/hardware behavior.
